title: VPC activation & post-upgrade readiness: API handshake, model warmup, and smokeburst validation
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Build and integrate a deterministic post-deployment readiness harness for Private (VPC) deployments that validates API handshake surface, model load stability, and a new 'smokeburst' synthetic workload to detect regressions in priming, KV cache behavior, and short-burst concurrency. This ticket wires the harness into the Terraform apply pipeline as an optional gate and documents runbook steps for on-call to triage failures.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible runbook exists that runs automatically after terraform apply and can also be triggered manually from CI/console
API handshake test passes across internal LB -> gateway -> runtime with TLS handshake and header propagation validated (status 200 and expected introspection header)
Model warmup sequence loads model weights and warms KV cache, and subsequent inference latency for a 128-token sequence stabilizes to within 20% of baseline within 60s
Smokeburst synthetic workload (10s bursts at 50rps, 3 iterations) completes without >1% 5xx errors and p50/p95 latency within configured SLO thresholds
Failure modes produce actionable diagnostics: last 50 traces, recent metric snapshots, and a link to the terraform apply run that caused the deploy
Harness artifacts (logs, traces, csv of latencies, and pass/fail summary) persist to the deployment artifacts bucket and are surfaced in the Console deployment detail page
tasks: Design smokeburst workload profile and target SLOs
Implement lightweight python harness for API handshake and model warmup (runtime-ready checks + sample prompt sequences)
Add KV cache warmup verification (hit-rate probe + counter diff) to the harness
Create a Terraform module hook that triggers harness post-apply and captures artifacts
Wire CI job and optional canary-run flag; avoid blocking critical infra apply in early rollout
Add Console UI link for artifacts and integrate with deployment timeline
Document runbook steps and triage checklist for OOS failures
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff - scoped requirements with PM and SRE. Agreed on three probes: handshake, warmup, smokeburst. Decided to keep initial run non-blocking with optional gate for high-risk upgrades.
2025-11-14: PoC harness implemented (python) that performs TLS handshake validation and simple /v1/health call; pushed PoC to infra repo: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/7890

2025-11-16: Discovered intermittent 502s in canary when concurrency ramped quickly; root cause traced to upstream proxy TLS renegotiation limits. Added staggered ramp and short jitter to smokeburst generator to avoid synchronized client bursts.

2025-11-18: KV cache probe added — instrumented runtime to emit kv_cache_stats; harness checks delta of hits/requests pre/post warmup. Baseline warmup time for default 7B model is ~22s in CI hardware.

2025-11-20: Terraform null_resource hook implemented and tested in staging. Harness uploads artifacts to s3://redwood-deploy-artifacts/private/vpc/ENG-421007/ and Console link shows in deployment timeline. Still flaky in one region due to NAT gateway connection limits; SRE investigating quota bump.
2025-11-20: Next: finalize canary gating policy, add alerting rule for smokeburst failures, and add e2e dashboard tile for quick pass/fail overview.
runbook_snippet: 1) Trigger: terraform apply completes and outputs deployment_id
3) Verify: harness exit code == 0 and artifacts present in S3 path shown in Console
4) If failing: collect last 50 traces (tracing service link), capture runtime logs (journalctl / container logs), gather terraform plan and apply outputs, and escalate to SRE oncall
5) Temporary mitigation: flip routing fallback policy to fallback-model-variant and re-run harness
notes: Design decision: smokeburst uses short bursts to surface cache-warmup and scheduling races that long steady-state load misses
We intentionally separate warm priming from steady-state performance tests to reduce noise in deploy gating
Consider adding a mode that simulates 'cold-client' behavior for private deployments with long-lived connections behind NAT gateways
Keep the initial Terraform hook non-blocking; enable blocking gate after 2 successful production rollouts
